name: Call of Duty: World at War

Optimal.Notes: The 2008 CoD engine is well within the Deck's capabilities at native resolution with medium-high settings; a 9 W TDP provides headroom for smooth, stable performance. In-game setting names are based on typical CoD engine options — verify exact names on first launch.

profiles.Summary: Call of Duty: World at War is a 2008 DirectX 9 title built on the CoD4 engine, which is very lightweight by modern standards and should run excellently on the Steam Deck's RDNA 2 GPU. Despite its "Unsupported" Deck rating (likely due to lacking native controller prompts or an online anti-cheat issue), ProtonDB gold-tier reports suggest it runs well under Proton with minor workarounds.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck reports were found; profiles are estimated from the game's very modest 2008 PC requirements and the Deck's hardware capability. On first launch, check that the game boots under Proton Experimental and confirm single-player works — online multiplayer may be blocked by PunkBuster anti-cheat.

MaxBattery.Notes: Runs at a reduced render resolution upscaled via FSR with a low TDP cap to maximise session length. In-game setting names are based on typical CoD engine options — verify exact names in the graphics menu on first launch.

KnownIssues: Game is rated Unsupported on Steam Deck, likely due to online anti-cheat (PunkBuster) blocking multiplayer — single-player and co-op should work fine.
Controller support is not officially listed; an on-screen keyboard or community controller layout may be needed for menus.
Some ProtonDB reporters note the game may require a specific Proton version to launch correctly.
No native Steam Deck controller prompts — Xbox/generic prompts will display instead.

MaxPerformance.Notes: This 2008 engine is light enough that the Deck can run it uncapped at max settings with no TDP limit; GPU and CPU are unlikely to be stressed. In-game setting names are based on typical CoD engine options — verify exact names on first launch.

Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at medium-high settings comfortably saturates the 60 Hz cap on this lightweight engine; 8 W TDP is enough headroom to avoid throttling during explosions. Depth of Field is left off to reduce GPU load and improve clarity.

profiles.Summary: Call of Duty: World at War is a 2008 Source-era (IW 3.0/id Tech derivative) title with very modest PC requirements, well within the Steam Deck's capabilities, though it carries an Unsupported Deck rating likely due to anti-cheat or launcher issues rather than raw performance. ProtonDB reporters rate it gold, suggesting it runs well with minor tweaks under Proton.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck-specific reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very modest 2008 PC requirements (GeForce 6600 minimum) and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU, which vastly exceeds those requirements. On first run, verify the game launches under GE-Proton and check whether PunkBuster blocks online play.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 5 W TDP and 600 MHz GPU clock this elderly engine runs cool and stable; FSR upscaling from 960x600 keeps the image acceptable. Multiplayer may be blocked by PunkBuster under Proton.

KnownIssues: Game is marked Unsupported on Steam Deck, possibly due to PunkBuster anti-cheat blocking multiplayer online sessions.
May require Proton Experimental or GE-Proton to launch correctly — default Proton has been inconsistent for some CoD titles.
Controller/gamepad support is not officially listed; on-screen keyboard or mouse emulation may be needed for menus.
Some users report the game's launcher or updater can hang; skipping the launcher via launch options may be necessary.

MaxPerformance.Notes: This 2008 engine has very low GPU overhead even at max settings; the RDNA 2 iGPU can push close to 90 fps at full resolution with no scaling needed. Battery drain is high at 15 W TDP, so this profile is best for docked or short sessions.
